guard: the user-mesh remedy states the omitted-scope default in full, `spawn,role:default`, rather than the narrower `spawn`
command: pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/manager build && pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/auth build && pnpm smoke:user-spawn:live
why: `csv` returns the default array verbatim when the flag is undefined. So omitting the flag hands
out TWO capabilities, and the second one is a DELEGATION capability.
The refusal's rationale sentence said `spawn` scope. That is a true-sounding claim that is
narrower than the thing it warns about, in the one sentence whose entire job is to make an
operator spell every field out. An operator who FOLLOWS the remedy passes `--scope ''` and is
safe; an operator who AUDITS a past omitted-scope grant against that sentence concludes it only
got `spawn` and closes a question that is still open. The falsehood is action-inverting in the
audit direction, not the paste direction.
WHY NO EXISTING CELL SAW IT. R1 and R2 grade the printed COMMAND and the ROW it writes. Nothing
read the RATIONALE, so six mutants across two configs stayed green with the wrong value shipped
in `dist/manager.js`. A sentence that no cell reads is not covered by the mutants around it.
The cell asserts the full value is present AND that the narrower claim is absent, because a
presence-only check would pass on text that still carried the short form elsewhere in the same
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY. The suite loads the manager from `implementations/manager/dist/index.js`, so
the command builds the manager before running and `afterRestore` rebuilds it, or a restored
source would sit behind a mutated dist and every later run would grade the wrong tree.
